title: Tears are mercy
hookLine: the Prophet ﷺ wept at his son's death, and called tears a mercy (Bukhari)
carry: the eyes weep, the tongue stays kind

cards: Even you, Messenger of Allah? The question comes from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, one of the Prophet's companions, and Anas ibn Malik tells it in Sahih al-Bukhari.
The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, had a baby son named Ibrahim, nursed in the house of a blacksmith's family. Anas remembers the Prophet taking the boy, kissing him, holding him close.
Some time later they went in again, and Ibrahim was dying. The Prophet's eyes filled, and the tears ran. His companion couldn't quite believe it.

teach.b: Some readers hear an old idea behind that question: the strong one doesn't cry, and whoever is closest to God should be calm, above all this. The Prophet's answer, in paraphrase, was simple: it is mercy.

teach.h: EYES WEEP, HEART GRIEVES, TONGUE IS KIND.
teach.b: Then he wept more, and said, again in paraphrase: the eyes shed tears and the heart grieves, but we say only what pleases our Lord, and we are saddened by your parting, Ibrahim. Three parts. The eyes are allowed to cry.
The heart is allowed to grieve. And the tongue is held: it says only what pleases God. The line isn't between crying and not crying.
It's between grief and protest. In another hadith in al-Bukhari, the Prophet's young grandchild is dying, and again his eyes overflow. Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah asks what this is.
The answer, paraphrased: this is mercy that Allah has put in the hearts of His servants, and Allah is merciful to those of His servants who are merciful. So tears aren't a weakness to be forgiven.
The same collection has the Prophet disowning, in paraphrase, those who slap their cheeks, tear their clothes and cry out with the wailing of the old days. Weeping, yes.
Wailing that rages against what God has decreed, no. A heart that breaks, and a tongue that stays kind.

how: Muslims weep openly at deaths and funerals, citing the Prophet's tears at his son Ibrahim's death, while avoiding loud wailing, tearing clothes and words of protest against God's decree; his words about the eyes, the heart and the tongue are often recalled.

o: grief should be hidden so others aren't burdened by it
crying for the dead earns them forgiveness from God
weeping in grief is a mercy God places in the heart

games.q: tears are mercy — tap the pairs.
p: says only what pleases the Lord

s: the Prophet held back his tears at his son's death
his eyes overflowed, and he called the tears mercy.
in al-Bukhari, the line is drawn at wailing, slapping cheeks and tearing clothes
weeping is mercy; raging against the decree is what's left behind.
the Prophet's grandchild's death is also told with his tears
Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah asked what this was, and was told it is mercy.

games.q: you're 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf. the Prophet, whom you've seen stay calm through everything, is weeping over his dying son. what do you do?
o: tell everyone to leave the room.
games.why: he asked, even you? and the Prophet answered: it is mercy, then said the eyes weep and the heart grieves.

practice: Is there a loss you've been holding tight, keeping composed about: a person, a place, a time of life? Let it come up gently; if tears come, they come, and if they don't, that's fine too, just don't push it back down.
If you pray, you can hold the Prophet's words: the eyes weep, the heart grieves, and the tongue says only what pleases the Lord.
If grief ever brings thoughts of harming yourself, please call or text 988 in the US, or your local emergency number.

wordCard.voice: Tears are mercy. The Prophet's answer when asked why he wept at his son's death: the tears are a mercy God places in the heart. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: mercy, the word the Prophet gave for his tears.

carryVoice: Your line: the eyes weep, the tongue stays kind. Even the Prophet's eyes filled for his son. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 1303 (Ibrahim's death; 'it is mercy'; the eyes shed tears and the heart grieves)
Sahih al-Bukhari 1284 (the grandchild; mercy Allah places in the hearts of His servants)
Sahih al-Bukhari 1294 (not of us who slaps cheeks, tears clothes, wails as in the days of ignorance)
